summary: Build skills taxonomies, gap analyses, and workforce plans in 5 days. Learn practical tools for HR, talent, and workforce strategy.
lede: Skills-based workforce planning helps you define critical capabilities, compare current workforce supply with future demand, and address gaps through development, redeployment, hiring, and succession actions. It connects workforce decisions to business priorities through practical tools such as skills taxonomies, competency frameworks, skills matrices, scenario plans, dashboards, and talent risk heat maps. This course shows you how to assess current skills, forecast future needs, evaluate build-buy-borrow options, and create a clear action roadmap for leadership. You will practise core planning exercises using realistic conditions such as incomplete job architecture, inconsistent skills data, competing hiring priorities, and limited reporting maturity, while exploring digital skills tools, HR analytics workflows, and AI-assisted talent insights at an overview level.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to connect workforce capability with business demand using practical skills-based planning methods.
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of HR operations, talent management, or workforce planning processes. Familiarity with job families, role profiles, headcount planning, and basic Excel-based analysis will help you move faster, but no coding is required. The course introduces AI-assisted skills inference and workforce analytics at an operational level, so you can apply the methods without programming or advanced statistics.
